note: Shoddy: poor-quality cloth made from recycled fibers.

anchor: rations not sound, or false in the measure
note: Contractors cheated sailors with rotten food and short measures.

anchor: impressment, for one thing, went on
note: Impressment: the practice of forcing men into the navy. It was a law and custom for centuries and continued through the Napoleonic wars.

anchor: judicially maintained by a Lord Chancellor as late as Mansfield
note: William Murray, Lord Mansfield (1705 to 1793), was a famous English judge who reshaped English law.

anchor: now fallen into a sort of abeyance
note: Abeyance: temporary disuse, set aside but not ended.
Abrogation: the official ending of a law or custom.

anchor: the more insatiate in demand for men
note: Insatiate: never satisfied. The navy always wanted more men.

anchor: against contingencies present and to come of the convulsed Continent
note: Contingencies: events that might happen. The Continent is mainland Europe, shaken by the revolution and war.

anchor: to shift his pennant from the Captain to the Theseus
note: A pennant is a long narrow flag flown on the ship carrying a commander. Moving it moved his command.

anchor: not indeed to terrorize the crew into base subjection
note: Subjection: control by force, as of an unwilling crew.

anchor: an allegiance if not as enthusiastic as his own
note: Allegiance: loyalty to a ruler or cause.

anchor: precautionary vigilance was strained against relapse
note: Relapse: a return to a worse state, here renewed mutiny.
A battery is a row of guns on one deck of a ship.

anchor: to stand with drawn swords behind the men working the guns
note: Officers feared mutiny in battle, so some stood behind the gun crews with swords out.
